NOTE: PROOF: push [BUG#9998 with doing/ row, no test; TASK#22 tip] -> "No test under the searched roots names: BUG-9998", rc=1. Also DoD.md:212-213 (§7).

RULE: The CI push check runs the subject check first, which refuses an empty or unreadable range rather than passing over nothing.
NOTE: PROOF: bash scripts/check-commit-subjects.sh --range HEAD..HEAD -> "range 'HEAD..HEAD' contains no commits — refusing." rc=1. Caveat: inside the workflow an empty (rollback) range exits 0 at :231 before it, and an unknown BEFORE (deadbeef...) is treated as a rewrite and checks the tip only (rc=0), so the refusal is effectively unreachable from the push step; by design since 27e79b9.

RULE: A new-branch push (all-zero before) checks the tip commit only and warns that coverage is partial.
NOTE: PROOF: BEFORE=0000... -> "::warning::new branch push: checking the tip commit only (partial coverage)", rc=0.

RULE: CI does not refuse a force push: a rollback to an earlier commit passes with a note; a history rewrite checks the tip only with a partial-coverage warning.
NOTE: PROOF: BEFORE=tip AFTER=base -> "force push back to an earlier commit: nothing new to check" rc=0; BEFORE=old tip, AFTER=rewritten tip -> "::warning::force push rewrote history: checking the tip commit only (partial coverage)" rc=0. Known limit: commits before the tip of a rewrite go unchecked.

RULE: A new item's row lands in doing/ with its first work commit; there is no separate filing or promotion commit.
NOTE: dod_stage_rows (dod-gate.sh:132) only fails when a row exists nowhere; a row outside doing/ is a note ("rows outside doing/: TASK-22(waiting-acceptance)" in the CI fixture run, rc=0). Neither "in doing/" nor "same commit" is checked, and the rule carries no *Judgement* label.

RULE: A review finding becomes work only if it is real and practical (observed, or on a core path with a realistic trigger); otherwise it is one "known limit" line; a reviewer's "push after these fixes" is input, not an order.
NOTE: Labelled *Judgement* (DoD.md:52).

RULE: The row moves to waiting-acceptance/ only once CI is green and never before the push; confirmed moves ride in the next ordinary work commit or lcm pass, never a separate commit per item.
NOTE: tests/lifecycle-docs checks folder consistency, not CI status or commit grouping. Unlabelled, so it reads as enforced.

RULE: lcm: lifecycle documents do not narrate status the folders already answer; where a second record is wanted, a test holds the two together.
NOTE: tests/lifecycle-docs and tests/doc-links hold existing second records together; nothing refuses a new narrated status. "Say something true" half is old D023.

RULE: A project's own permission rules go in tracked .claude/settings.project.json (host-specific ones in settings.local.json), never hand-edited into settings.json. Also DoD.md:176-177.

RULE: settings.project.json holds only permissions.allow/ask/deny/additionalDirectories; anything else (hooks, env) is refused, never merged or dropped.
NOTE: PROOF: project file {"hooks":{},...} -> "refuse: .claude/settings.project.json must be a JSON object holding only permissions.allow, ask, deny and additionalDirectories", rc=4.

RULE: blueprint pull lands settings.json as the blueprint's file with the project lists merged in, and drift compares that merged result.
NOTE: PROOF: project allow ["Bash(my-project-tool *)"] -> pull rc=0, landed allow contains it; vitest permission-policy "#6 drift judges the MERGED result" passed.

RULE: The blueprint's ask and deny always win: a project allow naming one is dropped, so a tightened rule cannot be re-allowed from a project.
NOTE: PROOF: project allow ["Bash(rm -rf /)" (deny), "Bash(git push --force*)" (ask), "Bash(my-project-tool *)"] -> landed allow keeps only ["Bash(my-project-tool *)"]. narrowed: exact-string match; a differently spelled allow covering the same command is not dropped (Claude Code still evaluates deny/ask first).

RULE: Never hand-edit settings.json for a project rule; the next pull refuses it until the rule moves to the project file.
NOTE: PROOF: see settings.project.json row: pull rc=4 "refuse: ... carries permission rules of its own"; drift lists it under "Cannot sync — pull refuses these until they are fixed: 1" (drift itself exited 0). narrowed: the refusal fires only when no settings.project.json exists; once one exists a hand edit is silently replaced by the merge, not refused.

RULE: blueprint drift exit 5 means the blueprint could not be read; it is not a clean report and never falls back to a local or cached copy.
